# The working note

This is a discussion example for a neighbourhood workshop. It records an idea and the questions to settle before a trial, rather than claiming that a lending service already exists.

## What we are trying to learn

The first question is not how large the inventory can become. It is whether people can find something useful, understand how to use it and return it without creating an unclear job for somebody else. A small trial gives the group a concrete situation to discuss.

A lending shelf and a repair session answer different needs. Borrowing helps with a task at home; a shared session makes room to ask questions. A travelling kit needs another arrangement again: somebody prepares it, transports it and checks it back in. The comparison table keeps these differences visible.

## What belongs in the first trial

Choose a modest selection with clear descriptions. Agree on who welcomes participants and who checks returned items. Record questions alongside the inventory instead of silently inventing rules after a problem occurs. Leave unsuitable tasks outside the trial.

Prepare a short introduction for the group, then keep this longer note available to anybody who needs the context. A participant who missed the meeting should still be able to understand what was proposed and what remains undecided.

## What to record afterwards

Keep observations separate from decisions. A question about a return slot is not evidence that the whole idea failed; a successful conversation is not proof that every lending arrangement will work. Record what was tried, the questions people asked and the next change the group agrees to test.

## Using this document

The cards provide an overview for a discussion. This note is the place for detail before and afterwards. On a small screen, use the reader menu to adjust presentation zoom or text fitting. In the comparison card, horizontal scrolling keeps the whole table accessible. The appearance chooser offers the themes included in this document.

Return to the site to explore how to write, organize or publish a similar project. The downloadable example includes the editable source, so you can replace this fictional brief with your own subject.
